NDT ERP for inspection companies in Joliet and Will County

A Joliet NDT company needs an ERP that can hold refinery, chemical, nuclear, rail and heavy civil work in one place, because the same crew might spend Monday on a unit at Channahon, Wednesday on structural steel for the I-80 rebuild and Friday on tank cars at an Elwood yard. The Atlantis ERP solution gives each of those its own job type, report format and cost centre, while keeping one record of who is certified for what, which instrument was calibrated when, and which procedure revision was in force.

The overview above covers the operators and codes in the Joliet corridor. This section is about the work behind the paperwork: how certifications, instruments, dispatch, reports, procedures, quotes and invoices actually run inside the Atlantis ERP, what is built in, what gets configured during implementation, and where it saves an inspection manager time on a normal week. It is written for owners, QA/QC managers and Level IIIs at small and mid-sized NDT contractors who are tired of running the business across spreadsheets, a shared calendar and an accounting package that never sees the job until the invoice.

If you want to see it working before you read further, ask for a Joliet-focused demo. Pricing is quote on request, sized to your headcount and the apps you actually use.

The I-80 rebuild and why heavy civil work belongs in the same system

The Illinois Department of Transportation's I-80 corridor rebuild through Joliet, a multiyear program covering roughly 16 miles from Ridge Road in Minooka to U.S. 30 in Joliet and New Lenox, is in its final phase. Its centrepiece is the replacement of the 1960s-era Des Plaines River bridges with two new, wider structures about 300 feet to the north, with traffic expected to move onto the new bridges during 2028 and the old spans to be demolished after that. For local NDT contractors, a job of that scale means years of weld inspection, fabrication-shop QC, and structural testing for fabricators and contractors across the supply chain.

Civil and bridge work runs to different rules from refinery work: different welding codes, different client paperwork, different owner representatives signing off, and often long, steady schedules rather than turnaround spikes. In the Atlantis ERP each project carries an NDT job type, site, client PO, contract, methods, codes, scope and acceptance criteria, plus assigned technicians and equipment. Project tasks carry method, technician, component, result, indication and defect counts, and procedure and WPS references. That structure lets you run a long bridge fabrication job alongside a two-week refinery outage without either one swallowing the other's data.

  • Refinery and chemical work: short, intense outages with many methods and heavy night-shift staffing.
  • Nuclear outage support: strict qualification records, radiation safety training and badge tracking for every technician.
  • Bridge and structural steel: weld inspection for fabricators and erectors on long schedules, with WPS references on every report.
  • Rail and tank car work: repeat inspections at intermodal and rail yards, often billed per unit or per day.

Technician certification tracking software built for a mixed Joliet workload

Technician certification tracking is a core app in the Atlantis ERP. Each certificate records the scheme (SNT-TC-1A, CP-189, ISO 9712, PCN, CSWIP or other), level from trainee to Level III, method, certifying body, issue, expiry and renewal dates, industry sector, OJT hours, training hours, exam result and attachments. Status is calculated automatically: active, expiring soon (within 90 days), expired or revoked, with Expiring Soon and Expired menus ready to open.

The industry sector field matters in Joliet more than in most places. A technician qualified under your written practice for refinery piping is not automatically the right person for a nuclear outage, where a client may require qualification under CP-189 and additional site training. Because each certificate carries its scheme and sector, a dispatcher can see at a glance who fits which job. The employee NDT profile adds highest level, methods certified, radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry, which is exactly the set of facts a plant access coordinator asks for before a nuclear or radiography job.

Vision tests record near vision (Jaeger J1 or J2), far vision, colour perception and contrast, with examiner, clinic, certificate file and expiry. Examination sheets store general, specific and practical scores against a passing score that defaults to 70 percent. Certificate templates per scheme hold validity in months, whether a vision test or exam is required, and minimum OJT and training hours. Daily checks raise warning tasks 90 days before any certificate or vision test lapses, email alerts go to the people you choose on the schedule you set, and timesheets warn when a technician's certificate is not valid at the time the hours are logged.

Calibration management software for Illinois winters and busy outage seasons

Asset Management tracks every instrument, probe and source-related item by serial number, with equipment type, assigned person, condition, asset tag, firmware, accessories, lifecycle state (new, active, in calibration, in repair, rented out, retired, disposed), calibration frequency and status. Calibration records hold the provider, certificate number, standard, range, uncertainty, accredited-lab flag, pass, fail or conditional result and next due date, and the calibration certificate register stores the lab accreditation number, validity status, PDF and expiry alerts.

Joliet winters are hard on equipment. Batteries, cables, probes and yokes all take a beating on open structures and outdoor pipe racks in January, and damage often gets noticed only when the next technician picks the kit up. The issue and return workflow, with supervisor and manager approval and condition recorded at both ends, puts a name and a date on every change in condition. The maintenance log records preventive, corrective, repair, cleaning, firmware update and probe replacement work with condition before and after, so a cracked cable or worn wedge becomes a record rather than a rumour.

Reservations block two jobs from claiming the same serial number, every movement in and out is logged, and dispatch warns you if an instrument on the job is out of calibration. Consumables such as penetrant, developer, cleaner, magnetic particle media, couplant and PPE have reorder levels and a low-stock flag. Purchase records mark vendors as OEM, dealer or calibration lab, store an accredited-lab flag with accreditation number and expiry, and link order lines to a specific equipment serial, so the cost of recalibrating one flaw detector is traceable to that unit.

Procedure control, including cold-weather limits

The Procedures app keeps your register: document number, revision, method (UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ET, TOFD, PAUT, LT, AE, hardness, PMI, CR, DR and more), scope, material, applicable standard such as ASME Section V, acceptance criteria, and the procedure text or an uploaded file. Procedures move through draft, submitted, reviewed, approved and published, with rejected and archived states, recorded rejection reasons, prepared, reviewed and approved-by names with dates, and locked approved revisions. A snapshot of each revision is kept.

Here is where that pays off in Illinois. ASME Section V sets a standard temperature range for liquid penetrant examination, and work outside it needs a procedure qualified for the lower or higher temperature. If your company has a separate cold-weather PT procedure, the register shows which revision was current, who approved it and when, and the report references it directly. When an auditor asks how a January PT on outdoor steel was done, you open the report, click through to the procedure and show the revision snapshot.

An AI-assisted first draft can speed up writing a new procedure and falls back to a built-in template if needed, but a Level III still reviews and approves it. Approvers receive email notifications and reminders for anything waiting on them, so procedures stop stalling for weeks in someone's inbox.

Crew dispatch and scheduling software for Joliet contractors

Team Assignments runs dispatch as a workflow: planned, dispatched, in field, submitted, closed. Each assignment carries the site's GPS coordinates and mobilisation and demobilisation dates, and you can manage it in calendar, kanban or list view. The technician availability calendar holds assigned, leave, training, sick and unavailable entries with overlaps blocked, and double-booking of technicians and equipment serial numbers is blocked outright.

For each technician you see status, current assignment, utilisation percentage and next available date. That makes the spring and fall outage crunch, when refinery, chemical and power clients all want crews at once, a planning problem you can see rather than a phone-tree scramble. Time Off feeds the same calendar, and Fleet records vehicle purpose, whether a vehicle can carry radioactive sources, the transport licence number and expiry, and assignment to project and driver with dates and mileage.

Timesheets record work type (inspection, travel, standby, setup), method, billable flag, rate multiplier, site, client, equipment serial and approval. Standby is worth tracking properly in this corridor: permit delays and unit holds at large plants are common, and standby that is not recorded on the day is standby you usually cannot bill.

NDT reporting software with 17 method-specific report types

Reporting is built into the Atlantis ERP and shares its engine with the standalone Digital Twin Reporting Software. It covers UT, RT, MT, PT, VT, ECT, IRIS, PAUT, MFL, TOFD, PWHT, PMI, hardness, UT thickness, ferrite, holiday/coating and computed radiography, each with its own numbering sequence.

Report data is method-specific: probe calibration tables for UT, source, technique, IQI type and placement for RT, technique and particle type for MT, method and developer for PT, focal laws for PAUT, scan mode and item lines for MFL, and thickness readings by direction for UTT. Weld and job lines carry defect type and orientation, and the overall result is acceptable, not acceptable, or acceptable with remarks. References to work order, request, WPS, contract, drawing numbers, procedure and standard sit on every report, which suits bridge and fabrication clients who check the WPS on every weld.

The workflow runs draft, in progress, review, approved, sent, with inspector, reviewer and approver signatures and fields for a third-party or authorized inspector. Versioned company templates in Excel, Word, PDF or HTML carry your logo and headers, and Excel templates fill automatically by mapping fields to cells. The offline field app works without signal, stores drafts and photos locally, captures on-screen signatures, previews the PDF and syncs later.

NDT quoting and invoicing software for per-day, per-unit and per-job work

Quotations carry job type, site, project dates and applicable codes, NDT service products flagged by method and category, a global discount, and a branded PDF. Clients can accept and sign online and the quote converts to a sales order. Invoices carry NDT project, job or PO number, site, invoice type and industry sector, with subtotals for labour, equipment and consumables, and lines that record cost centre, method, equipment serial, technician, rate type and days or hours.

That mix covers the ways Joliet work is actually billed: day rates on outages, unit-based work at rail yards, and lump-sum or milestone work on fabrication packages. Billable timesheet hours and their multipliers feed invoicing directly, and field expenses and per diems recorded in Expenses can be re-billed to the job. Taxes, payments and reminders are configured for Illinois during implementation. The financial dashboard shows revenue, cost of sales, gross margin, operating expenses, EBITDA, outstanding invoices, bills and expenses over 12 months. To get a scoped figure for your team, request a quote.

Integrations and the wider Atlantis stack

The Atlantis ERP has an open REST API and integrates with SAP, Maximo, NetSuite, QuickBooks or any system that accepts API connections, scoped per implementation. A second REST API serves field devices: jobs assigned to a technician, equipment issued to them, report submission and sync. Dashboards show calibration due and overdue, certificates expiring and expired, and issued equipment overdue for return, next to the financial view. Company certifications such as your ISO registration are tracked with their own alert days.

The CRM records service line, lead source, NDT service type, industry sector, site country and estimated technicians and days, with a 0 to 100 NDT lead score. Business cards collected at trade events can be photographed and turned into leads, and AI marketing tools draft campaign emails and drip sequences that can run on your own server. For plant owners who want inspection results in 3D, Atlantis Digital Twins maps indications and damage onto the asset model and trends thickness and remaining life. Technicians can practise on the Practical NDT 3D simulator, and the full list of modules is on the ERP apps page, including certificates and team assignments.

Getting started with a Joliet implementation

Most Joliet contractors start with certifications and calibration, because those are the records every refinery, chemical and nuclear client checks first. We load your technicians, certificates, vision tests and instruments, set alert recipients and look-ahead periods, and switch on the dispatch checks. Reporting templates, the offline app, procedures, quoting and invoicing follow, and integrations come last once the underlying data is clean. Atlantis NDT founder Anoop Rayavarapu, an ASNT NDT Level III, reviews the NDT-specific configuration. Book a scoping call to start.

Frequently asked questions

What is the best NDT ERP for a small Joliet inspection company?

For a small company, the best fit is one affordable, customizable system that joins certifications, calibration, dispatch, reports and invoicing. The Atlantis ERP solution does that and is scoped to your size with a quote on request.

Can it track CP-189 and SNT-TC-1A certifications side by side?

Yes. Each certificate records its scheme, level, method, sector and dates, so a technician can hold several and the dispatcher sees which ones apply to a given job.

Does it record radiation badge numbers for RT and nuclear work?

Yes. The employee NDT profile stores radiation safety training, radiation badge number and medical fitness expiry alongside certifications.

Can we run bridge fabrication work and refinery outages at the same time?

Yes. Separate job types, projects and cost centres keep each stream's scope, reports and margins apart while sharing one pool of technicians and equipment.

Does it calculate inspection due dates for client plant equipment?

No. The ERP manages your company's operations, people, instruments, procedures, reports and billing. Atlantis offers API 510, 570 and 653 inspection services separately through inspection services.

Can we keep our current accounting package?

Yes. The open REST API connects to QuickBooks, NetSuite, SAP or any system that accepts API connections, scoped during implementation.

Is training available for our technicians?

Atlantis offers ASNT SNT-TC-1A-based NDT training, and the ERP's eLearning portal can host your own Level I, II and III course content with quizzes and completion certificates.
